Aditya / Lauren — see answers inline and attached excerpt. Summary: 

- Audit rights: Our standard DPA allows for remote evidence review through the Redwood Evidence Portal (timeboxed, access-controlled, and auditable). On-site audits are permitted for enterprise customers but require a breaches/operational-impact clause to be met and a scheduling lead time of 6+ weeks; we also charge for third-party auditor facilitation when specialized access is required. We can offer a hybrid approach (remote first, on-site if gaps remain).

- Art.30: Attached is a redacted excerpt from our processing register (art30-redwood-excerpt-20261202.pdf). It includes high-level categories, subprocessors, and legal bases; all production hostnames and customer IDs are redacted.

- Subprocessors: We maintain two curated lists: telemetry/logging processors (analytics, monitoring) and data processors (model serving, embeddings store). We can provide the telemetry-only list up front and include the full processor inventory under NDA or via the evidence portal.

- KMS/residency & deletion: For Private deployments, customers may supply/manage their CMKs (bring-your-own-key). For Redwood-managed keys, keys are stored in our KMS in the region of the deployment (we can provide attestation of key wrapping). Proof-of-deletion: we provide retention/deletion logs and signed attestations for deletion events; for derivatives we capture the deletion action and token-level deletion traces where feasible.

Attached: art30-redwood-excerpt-20261202.pdf

3) If ClearView wants an on-site option, we will require scope confirmation and an amendment to the procurement SOW.
